[[Category:Schwenkfelders, Palatine Migrants]] [[Category: Harpersdorf, Thüringen]] [[Category:St. Andrew, Arrived 12 September 1734]] {{Palatine Migration}} == Biography == '''David Hubner/Heebner''' was born in 1696. He married Maria Kriebel. In 1734, David (E21) and Maria (E85) boarded the ''St Andrew'' with other Schwenkfelder immigrants headed to Pennsylvania with their sons Christopher (E87) and Balthasar E212), as well as David's brother Hans Hubner (E74) and half sister Maria Wiegner Hubner (E117). Their son Bathasar died on the journey and was buried at sea.
On the 3rd [of August], David Hübner’s youngest child died, aged 1 year, 20 weeks, and was buried at sea according to the ship’s custom, formerly mentioned, somewhere off the coast of Spain. The hymn “Ach wie elend ist unsre Zeit,” (Oh, how bitter is our journey!) was sung.
The captain's list for the St Andrew which arrived in Philadelphia on 12 Sept 1734 from Rotterdam records four men "Melchior Hiebner," "Georg Hiebner," "David Hiebner, sick" and "Johannes Hiebner," and women and children:"Maria Heibner," a second "Maria Heibner," "Christopher Hiebner," and third variant spelling "Maria Hiebner," "Anna Hiebner," "Hans Hiebner" '''Emigration''': Strassburger, Ralph Beaver, 1883-1959., ''Pennsylvania German pioneers; a publication of the original lists of arrivals in the port of Philadelphia from 1727 to 1808 ... Edited by William John Hinke ... v.42''
Norristown, Pa., Pennsylvania German Society, 1934; page: 136
[https://hdl.handle.net/2027/inu.30000007109121?urlappend=%3Bseq=208%3Bownerid=13510798895990661-212 HathiTrust] (accessed 21 July 2025) When arrived at the Port of Philadelphia in September 1734, Names of Foreigners Who Took the Oath of Allegiance to the Province and State Pennsylvania, 1727-1775. Page 107 & 108. www.ancestry.com: Names of Foreigners David was on the sick list and Maria was expecting as their daughter Susanna was born in October 1734. Their children Rosanna and George were born a few years later. In 1736, David acquired land in Frederick Township and eventually acquired land in Worcester Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. David died in 1784 and was buried in the Salford Schwenkfelder Cemetery, where his wife joined him in 1793. Find a Grave, database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/27678574/david-heebner: accessed June 24, 2024), memorial page for David Heebner (27 Aug 1696–27 Dec 1784), Find a Grave Memorial ID 27678574, citing Salford Schwenkfelder Cemetery, Harleysville, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, USA; Maintained by Tom Myers (contributor 47272121). ==Research Notes== ===Schwenkfelder Emigrant=== ''DAVID HÜBNER (HEEBNER)''' is identified as '''[E 21]''' (Emigrant Number) in the book ''[https://archive.org/details/genealogicalreco00unse/page/301/mode/1up The genealogical record of the Schwenkfelder families : seekers of religious liberty who fled from Silesia to Saxony and thence to Pennsylvania in the years 1731-1737]'' published in 1923.
See: [[Space:Schwenkfelders, Palatine Migrants, 1731 - 1737|Schwenkfelders, Palatine Migrants, 1731 - 1737]]
'''[21] DAVID HUBNER (HEEBNER) [E 21],''' '''DAVID HUBNER (HEEBNER) [E 21]''': ''The genealogical record of the Schwenkfelder families : seekers of religious liberty who fled from Silesia to Saxony and thence to Pennsylvania in the years 1731-1737''
1923; page: 301
[https://archive.org/details/genealogicalreco00unse/page/301/mode/1up Internet Archive] (accessed 28 November 2025) b Aug. 27, 1696; d Dec. 27, 1784; m MARIA KRIEBEL [E 85], b Jan., 1705; d June 11, 1793; dau Balthasar Kriebel; according to Schneider (p 77b , 64b) they were married by Regent. David Hübner was a brother of Hans Hübner [E 74] and also half brother to Maria Wiegner Hübner [E 117]. In 1774 Maria, wife of David Hüibner, wrote to her sister Regina, wife of Christoph Groh in Silesia, that she was then 70 years of age. On Feb. 21, 1769, Maria Hübner and “Schwager” David Hiibner wrote a letter to “Schwager Christoph Groh und Schwester Regina, Susanna und Anna wde auch Christ ihr man,” in which they state that Maria, wife of David Hübner for the past ten years has been suffering with a sore leg, and regarding further particulars they state that ‘‘this spring it will be three years that we left our former home, and we now live between two of our children in Worcester Twp. Our eldest son Christ married Hans Wiegner’s daughter, and lives about a mile from us and they have four children. Susan, our elder daughter, is married to Christ Wagner, eldest son of widow Anna Wagner. They live a mile above us and have three children. A year ago, on New Year’s day, they lost a young child.”
“The other daughter, Rosina, has a second husband, viz., Baltzaar Jackel, eldest son of the late Abraham Jackel. They have three children and live in Skippack. The other child, our youngest, named George, is still single and lives with us.” (Translation.)
In this same letter they also send greetings to Abr. Hübner, brother of David, also to “Christ Wag.” and his daughters.
David Hübner came to Pa. in 1734, with his wife and son Christoph. He was sick upon his arrival in Phila. (c/. signature list). In 1736 he acquired land in Frederick Twp. [Plate E IV], and after pur¬ chasing several other tracts (c/. Haynes of Immigrants), acquired a tract in Worcester Twp. [Plate G VI], owned (1920) by Jeremiah K. Anders. David Hübner was naturalized Sept. 24, 1745. Both he and his wife are buried in Salford Schw. Cem.

5733020.bio:
== Biography ==

Susanna's parents David Hebner/Heebner and Maria Kriebel were immigrants E21 and E85 in the Schwenkfelder migration.  They arrived in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania in September 1734 with their son Christopher E87.  Susanna was born in October 1734.

Susanna
<ref>The Genealogical record of the Schwenkfelder families : seekers of religious liberty who fled from Silesia to Saxony and thence to Pennsylvania in the years 1731-1737. New York: Rand McNally & Co., 1923. Family 196-1 on page 1502 and family unit 21 on page 270.</ref>
 married Christopher Wagener/Wagner on November 26, 1754.  They lived in Worcester Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania having 4 children, one of which, a daughter died young.  

The Genealogical Record of Schwenkfelder families says that she was buried in a private cemetery on the Heebner farm.  She is buried in a small cemetery now known as Wagner Cemetery or Christopher Wagner Burying Ground on Heebner Road in Worcester, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. Christopher Wagner bought land from John K Heebner, so this land may have been known as Heebner farm. It is also possible that this cemetery is on land that was owned by the Heebner family since both the Heebner and Wagner families owned land in Worcester Township.
<ref>Find a Grave, database and images (https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/28183594/susanna-wagner: accessed June 24, 2024), memorial page for Susanna Heebner Wagner (Oct 1734–2 Jul 1817), Find a Grave Memorial ID 28183594, citing Christopher Wagner Burying Ground, Worcester, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, USA; Maintained by Tom Myers (contributor 47272121).</ref>

Thank you to [[Schultz-1144 | Rod Schultz]] for creating WikiTree profile Heebner-9 through the import of Alfa.GED on May 13, 2013. Click to the Changes page for the details of edits by Rod and others.

Research notes:
Susanna is a descendent of the Schwenkfelders who immigrated to Pennsylvania in the 1730's.  Many of these immigrants have similar names and intermarrying families.  I plan to come back to this page and add her parents, siblings, and children. But if someone wants to update this before I get back to this page then I recommend looking at the Genealogical Record of Schwenkfelder families 1923 edition.
Susanna's parents are immigrants E21, David Hubner/Heebner and E85, Maria Kriebel, on page 270 (in volume 1 of 1923 edition). Susanna's husband is Christopher Wagener/Wagner E197.  Susanna and her husband's family unit is 196-1 on page 1502 (in volume 2 of 1923 edition)

== Biography ==
{{1776 Sticker|rank=Private| unit=4th Battalion, Philadelphia County Militia, Pennsylvania Militia, American Revolution}} 
{{NSSAR Patriot Ancestor|sar-number=179153  |rank=Private}}

"David Huebner or Heebner and his wife Maria, came to Pennsylvania in 1734. Their son, George Heebner, born in 1744, married Susanna Heydrick, and their only child, Rev. Baltzer Heebner, was born June 12, 1770."

George Kriebel Heebner was 39 when he died. He is buried in the Towamencin Schwenkfelder Cemetery, Lansdale, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, USA.  (Montgomery  county was created on September 10, 1784, out of land originally part of Philadelphia County.)
